title: Conforming Alternate Versions & Page Variations
wcag22Concept: WCAG 2.2 Conformance Requirement 5.2.2 permitted non-accessible web pages if an accessible 'Conforming Alternate Version' (a secondary accessible page with identical information) was provided.
plainEnglishSummary: WCAG 2.2 Conformance Requirement 5.2.2 permitted a qualifying Conforming Alternate Version under defined W3C conditions (see W3C CAV Definition). WCAG 3 draft proposals phase out secondary fallback pages in favor of requiring the primary digital asset itself to be natively accessible across user variations.
workingGroupDebate: W3C AGWG members broadly agree that alternate versions lead to stale, poorly maintained secondary experiences that stigmatize disabled users. Current W3C discussions focus on page variations (e.g. responsive breakpoints) rather than allowing separate fallback pages.

debateLinks.title: W3C WCAG 3 GitHub Discussion #623: Conforming Alternate Versions in WCAG 3

inclusionLikelihood: Extremely Low (<5% for alternate versions; Page Variations under review)

personaImpact.designer: Design primary UI components to be natively accessible. Do not rely on 'text-only' toggles.
personaImpact.developer: Build a single, inclusive codebase. Avoid routing screen reader users to a separate accessible domain.
personaImpact.qa: Audit the main user flow. Alternate version pages no longer grant conformance.
personaImpact.productManager: Budget for primary product accessibility rather than secondary fallback maintenance.

title: Page-by-Page Binary Pass/Fail Conformance
wcag22Concept: WCAG 2.2 evaluates accessibility on a strict page-by-page basis (either a whole URL passes 100% of SCs at Level AA or the entire page fails).
wcag3Status: Replaced by Task & Outcome Scoring Model
plainEnglishSummary: WCAG 2.2 treated accessibility as a pass/fail checklist for individual URLs. WCAG 3 replaces this with continuous scoring across entire user tasks and processes, allowing organizations to measure incremental progress.
workingGroupDebate: Discussions center on how to prevent single minor bugs from declaring a massive enterprise web app '100% non-compliant' while still ensuring critical user tasks can be completed.

inclusionLikelihood: Extremely Low (<10% for binary page pass/fail)

personaImpact.designer: Focus on user flow journeys (e.g. registration to checkout) rather than isolated page screens.
personaImpact.developer: Ensure complete end-to-end task flows operate smoothly without blocking friction.
personaImpact.qa: Report accessibility health scores across complete user journeys rather than single-page pass/fail lists.
personaImpact.productManager: Track accessibility maturity scores and task completion metrics in quarterly OKRs.

title: Strict A / AA / AAA Conformance Levels
wcag22Concept: WCAG 2.2 categorizes all criteria into rigid buckets: Level A (minimum), Level AA (standard target for legal compliance), and Level AAA (enhanced).
wcag3Status: Replaced by Rating Levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold)
plainEnglishSummary: The traditional A/AA/AAA tier structure from WCAG 2.x is omitted in WCAG 3. Instead, WCAG 3 uses rating levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold) based on total outcome points, automated testing, and user testing assertions.
workingGroupDebate: Significant debate exists around legal adoption and how regulators (like the US DOJ or EU European Accessibility Act) will map WCAG 3 rating levels to statutory compliance thresholds.

personaImpact.qa: Evaluate assertions and functional outcome coverage rather than AA checklists.
personaImpact.productManager: Prepare compliance roadmaps for outcome-based scoring systems.

title: Page-Level 'Accessibility Supported' Reliance
wcag22Concept: WCAG 2.2 allowed authors to rely on specific user agent/assistive technology combinations defined in an author-specified 'accessibility supported' baseline.
plainEnglishSummary: In WCAG 2.2, authors could claim compliance if a feature worked in one specific screen reader/browser combination listed in their conformance claim. WCAG 3 shifts responsibility toward broad, platform-agnostic interoperability.
workingGroupDebate: W3C working group is defining standardized expectations for modern browsers, mobile OSs, and assistive technology interfaces to eliminate narrow vendor exemptions.

personaImpact.designer: Design for cross-platform assistive technology compatibility.
personaImpact.developer: Use standard ARIA and HTML specs that work across VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS, and TalkBack.
personaImpact.qa: Test across multiple browser/screen reader combinations.
personaImpact.productManager: Ensure multi-device and multi-AT support in platform support matrix.
